articles.title: Central Ministry removes Mahadayi basin works from online queue of pending projects
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Union government has removed the Banduri Nala diversion project in the Mahadayi river basin from the list of pending clearances from the website of the Forest Ministry.
This is believed to be due to Karnataka government’s delay in submitting responses to some queries raised by the Central team about the project.
The project was removed from the online queue of pending proposals on the PARIVESH portal of the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC).

Karnataka Neeravari Nigam Limited (KNNL) had applied for clearance to divert 71 acres of forest land for construction of pipelines, a pumphouse and powerlines in Nerse, Manturga and Bacholi villages and surrounding areas in Khanapur of Belagavi district.
Farmers, who received notices, held a meeting in Khanapur and opposed the land acquisition proposal in April 2025.
The Ministry officials conducted two field visits and issued a notice to the Congress government in the State in July 2026. But this notice did not receive an appropriate response on time.
The Central Ministry officials also indicated that a final decision on the proposal can be taken only after the Supreme Court gives a ruling in the inter-State river water dispute.

This is the first phase of the Mahadayi basin diversion works planned to provide drinking water to Hubballi-Dharwad and Gadag cities and also, some villages. The proposal for the Kalasa Nala diversion project, which is another project, is yet to be submitted to the Centre.
Karnataka forest officials say that the Banduri Nala involves lesser area of forest land submersion, compared to the Kalasa Nala project.
Meanwhile, Goa Water Resources Development Minister Subhash Shirodkar said that the Union government has withdrawn forest clearance given to Karnataka’s proposal.
He told reporters in Panaji on Friday that this move is in favour of Goa and it will strengthen his State’s case in the Supreme Court against the river basin diversion projects.
He welcomed the move and argued that Goa is opposed to the river basin projects as they can threaten the Mhadei Wildlife Sanctuary and Western Ghats ecology in general.

1. Core Context & Background: The Union government has removed the Banduri Nala diversion project in the Mahadayi river basin from the list of pending clearances from the website of the Forest Ministry.

2. Key Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: This is believed to be due to Karnataka government’s delay in submitting responses to some queries raised by the Central team about the project. The project was removed from the online queue of pending proposals on the PARIVESH portal of the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC).

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He welcomed the move and argued that Goa is opposed to the river basin projects as they can threaten the Mhadei Wildlife Sanctuary and Western Ghats ecology in general.

articles.title: Ploughing through the red tape: Inside Ambati Rayudu’s mission to fix Hyderabad cricket
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Hyderabad cricket has heard many speeches, but few came with a tractor.

In the six months since Ambati Rayudu promised to change the culture, the former India batter has been spotted pitch-side at dawn, at a soil vendor’s door in the rain and, by his own count, five to seven kilos lighter.

The initial results suggest that the effort is paying off. The first phase of this Ranji Trophy season has concluded with Hyderabad winning three matches and playing out one draw, enough to put them on top of the Elite Group B table with 20 points. The satisfaction is evident, from players to coaches.

Rayudu, the Director of Cricket Operations at the Hyderabad Cricket Association (HCA), shares that satisfaction but remains wary of premature celebrations. He takes greater pride in the systems being put in place.

“I wouldn’t read too much into the results as of now, but I’m very happy with the way the systems are set. And most importantly, the boys are very confident and glad there is something to look forward to,” he told The Hindu.

It is a long way from May 5, when he walked into a hall of cameras and vowed to take Hyderabad cricket to the next level. Plenty of people have made similar promises in those corridors. What followed, Rayudu says, was quieter than the announcement: getting the basics right, every single day.

First, he filled the calendar. Hyderabad’s age-group sides now play far more matches than the league demands, with close to a thousand match days scheduled this season. It is how his own generation grew up.
“When they wake up, if they don’t have a game, they need to be worried: ‘What am I going to do today?’ We wanted to get that feeling back.”

Wasim Jaffer’s arrival as mentor has reinforced the change, helping build a cricketing culture among players and coaches alike. Open trials now allow district players to walk into Gymkhana and compete for a State cap.
From the grassroots to the selection room, no corner of the system has escaped a rethink.

“The first point on our agenda while picking selectors was: Do they have the integrity required? Because beyond that, we will take care of whatever comes. And because they come with such integrity, they are quite adamant and stubborn in their decision making as well. That is a welcome sign because we don’t want them to be yes-men. And they have done a fantastic job, so no complaints at all. All due credit to Jeevan Reddy (HCA secretary) or anybody else, they have never questioned the team selections.”
His Cricket Operations Committee (COC) has stepped in only when it comes to choosing the team’s leadership.

articles.title: Malappuram teachers to take part in football championship to raise awareness of drug abuse
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Twenty teams of teachers from across Malappuram district will take part in the district teachers’ sevens football championship to be held at Thalappara near Tirurangadi on Saturday (November 14). Organised by the Tirurangadi Teachers’ Squad, the tournament aims to spread awareness against drug abuse and encourage students to take up sports and lead healthy lives.

The championship carries the slogan, ‘Wear boots against drugs, make football your passion’. It is being organised in support of the State government’s anti-drug campaign Operation Toofan. The organisers said teachers should not only advise students to stay away from drugs but also set an example by taking part in sports and promoting healthy habits.
The tournament will also bring teachers from different educational institutions together and promote friendship, unity and sportsmanship.

articles.title: Koti Deepotsavam begins today, continues till November 30
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The annual Koti Deepotsavam of Bhakti TV will be held at NTR Stadium near Indira Park from November 14 to 30, coinciding with the auspicious Kartika Masam.

The 17-day spiritual event will be held every day from 5.30 p.m. to 10 p.m., bringing together prominent Jagadgurus, heads of various religious institutions and renowned spiritual speakers, including Chaganti Koteswara Rao and Garikapati Narasimha Rao.

Devotees will have the opportunity to participate in special rituals and perform pujas themselves. The festival will also feature celestial wedding ceremonies of festival deities from several prominent temples.

Among the major attractions will be Maha Shankhabhishekam, Bhasmabhishekam of Ujjain Mahakaleshwar, special worship of the Somnath Jyotirlinga and darshan of the deities of Kolhapur Mahalakshmi, Kanchi Kamakshi and Madurai Meenakshi temples.
Entry to the event will be free. The organisers said all essential materials required for the rituals, including wicks, oil and earthen lamps, would also be provided to devotees free of cost.

articles.title: Modi recalls Mysuru Wadiyars’ contribution to science and education
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said Mysuru had a rich tradition of establishing institutions that promote knowledge, education and research, recalling the contribution of the erstwhile Mysuru rulers in building the foundation for scientific advancement.

Speaking after inaugurating the COSMOS Mysuru LED Dome Planetarium here, he said the University of Mysore was established during the reign of Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar. The Wadiyar family also played a significant role in the establishment of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) in Bengaluru. These institutions had provided generations of students and researchers with opportunities to excel, he said.

At a time when India was achieving one milestone after another in science, Mysuru was adding a new chapter to the country’s scientific journey through the state-of-the-art COSMOS Planetarium, Mr. Modi said.
“The planetarium is being dedicated today. It is India’s first LED Dome Planetarium. I had the opportunity to watch a show here. It was a remarkable experience,” he said.

Drawing a parallel between the Viveka Smaraka, which he inaugurated during his previous visit, and India’s first LED Dome Planetarium, Mr. Modi said the two institutions reflected India’s traditions of spirituality and science. While the Viveka Smaraka encouraged people to look within and explore spiritual knowledge, the planetarium inspired them to look towards the skies and understand the vast universe. “Spirituality and science have always progressed together,” he said.

Calling upon the COSMOS Planetarium authorities to encourage students to visit and experience the facility, he said, “Some of the children who visit the planetarium may one day return here to tell us about their achievements. That will be the biggest achievement of COSMOS,” he said.

Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Nirmala Sitharaman and Chief Minister D K Shivakumar also spoke. Governor Sudha Yadav, Mysuru and Kodagu MP Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar and Minister for Higher Education Basavaraj Rayareddi were present.
Earlier, Mr. Modi paid his respects to Goddess Chamundeshwari and greeted the people of Mysuru.

articles.title: Vigilance detects irregularities at Kasaragod port office
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Four alleged irregularities, including unauthorised appointments, diversion of sand permits, use of boats with expired licences for sand mining, and discrepancies in financial records, were detected during a Vigilance inspection at the Kasaragod Port Office.

The Vigilance team found that employees had been appointed on a daily wage basis without government orders or approval from the competent authorities since 2017. Such employees had been deployed for work at river ghats as well as the port office. The team examined documents relating to these appointments.

The inspection also revealed that sand had been allotted to individuals using building permits without the knowledge or consent of the actual owners. Permits issued in the name of building owners were allegedly used by other persons to obtain sand.

Another irregularity concerned licences for boats used for sand mining at authorised ghats. The team found that the validity of the licences of boats currently being used for sand mining had expired on August 31, 2026. The circumstances under which boats with expired licences continued to be used for the activity were examined.

The fourth irregularity involved discrepancies in the cash book of the office. The cash book had been updated only up to August 14, 2026, with financial transactions for nearly three subsequent months remaining unrecorded.
The Vigilance authorities are scrutinising the findings and documents collected to initiate further action.

articles.title: India's exports up 29.9% in October; trade deficit narrows to $20.09 billion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India’s merchandise exports rose to an all-time high of $49.5 billion in October 2026, bringing down the country’s overall trade deficit, official data released on Friday showed.
While a large part of this growth was due to petroleum products, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said diversification of exports to various locations helped improve the numbers.
India’s total exports, including goods and services, stood at $89.99 billion in October 2026, up nearly 30% from last October.
The overall trade deficit shrank from $25.1 billion last October to $20.1 billion year-on-year.

“In the month of October, the exports of merchandise exports have registered a new peak of $49.47 billion,” Mr. Agrawal said at a press briefing. “This is the highest-ever monthly merchandise export value, along with the highest monthly growth of 45.03% in the last five years.”
Merchandise imports rose to a record high of $89.35 billion in October 2026, up 16.5% YoY. Total imports stood at $110.1 billion, a 16.6% increase.

According to trade experts, goods exports growing faster than merchandise imports shows that while the rise in global prices contributed to the increase in the value of India’s exports, there was also an increase in the underlying export volumes.

“The particularly encouraging part of this growth is that this is not in any particular sector, this is not in any particular geography, it is broad-based across countries and regions,” Mr. Agrawal added. “43 of our 50 top export destinations posted positive growth in October 2026 as compared to 2025.”
The data show that India’s exports to 12 out of its top 20 export destinations grew by double digits or more.
Mr. Agrawal pointed out that India’s exports to its free trade agreement (FTA) partners had grown strongly.
One of the key areas of diversification has been the African continent, with exports to that region growing 44% in April-September 2026 to $31.4 billion.
Notably, India’s trade with West Asia is recovering as countries find alternate routes and ports other than those along the constrained Strait of Hormuz.

fullParagraphs: The story so far: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reportedly proposed to the Ministry of Finance tightening the limits of the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), in an attempt likely aimed at preventing a massive outflow of dollars from India. Under the current structure, Indian residents can remit up to $250,000 (over ₹2 crore) in a financial year for purposes such as travel, education, medical treatment, and overseas investments.

The LRS is a scheme under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), introduced by the RBI in 2004. It covers both capital account and current account transactions. Under the capital account, transactions are permitted for opening overseas foreign currency bank accounts, purchasing property, extending interest-free loans of up to one year, and investing in foreign equity, mutual funds, and listed debt securities.

articles.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

articles.title: How did a tax proposal lead the Dutch government to the verge of collapse? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Story so far: The Dutch government came close to a collapse this week over its Tax Plan for 2027 as members of the three-party ruling coalition disagreed over an amendment to the plan. Though the plan was passed in the lowest-possible majority in the House of Representatives on Thursday (November 12, 2026) night and the government subsequently defeated a no-confidence motion, the developments have brought a rift in the coalition out in the open and threaten the future of the government led by Rob Jetten just nine-months into its 4-year term.

The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house. The centrist D66 led by Prime Minister Jetten, the youngest premier in the country’s history, is the single largest party with 26 seats and is joined by centre-right parties People’s Party for Freedom and Democracy (VVD) and Christian Democratic Appeal (CDA), with 22 and 18 seats respectively. The government came to power in February, 117 days after a snap election in October last year necessitated by the collapse of Dick Schoof’s right-wing government as far-right leader of Freedom Party Geert Wilders withdrew his support. The months following the election that failed to produce a clear winner saw parties across political spectrum and ideologies negotiate to form a government to no effect, paving the way for the centrist parties to make do with a minority administration.

articles.title: India needs to create high-quality jobs, increase productivity growth: IMF
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment and faster creation of high-quality jobs to achieve the medium-term potential growth of 6.8%, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Thursday (November 12, 2026).
In its October World Economic Outlook, the IMF had upgraded India’s medium-term potential growth to 6.8% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%.

The upgrade took into account a few factors, including favourable demographics, a large and growing domestic economy or domestic market for goods, and continued momentum on structural reforms, Julie Kozack, Communications Director, IMF, told reporters in Washington.

“But in general, like in many countries, we are encouraging India to take continuing reforms, particularly to focus on how productivity growth can be increased,” she said in response to a question from PTI .
The IMF official said that to further the medium-term potential, India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment, and faster creation of high-quality jobs.
Ms. Kozack said these issues will come up during the Article 4 consultations with India.
Last month, the IMF raised India’s growth forecast for fiscal year 2027 and fiscal year 2028 to 7%, from the 6.4% and 6.7% projections respectively made in July.
“India does remain a key growth engine for the world. The economy has strong fundamentals and has shown considerable resilience,” Ms. Kozack said.

articles.title: CAG widens purview of power sector audit, starting with DISCOMs; consumer satisfaction in focus
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) is undertaking a comprehensive audit of the power sector, beginning with distribution companies (discoms), where consumer satisfaction, power trading and financial sustainability emerging as key focus areas.

The exercise will subsequently cover transmission, generation, renewable energy and the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), with each segment’s operational and financial performance being assessed over the preceding five years, according to officials familiar with the development.

Discoms will be the first to be audited, with the ongoing phase covering their performance between FY21 and FY26. As many as 39 discoms across the country, along with five departmental undertakings, will be assessed. Privately owned discoms, however, will remain outside the scope of the exercise.
The audit commenced in July this year, with the report expected to be finalised around the middle of the next financial year. The audit of the transmission segment is scheduled to begin with FY27.
Moving beyond conventional financial and operational assessments, the CAG has directed auditors to engage directly with electricity consumers, local experts and influential groups..
“We told our auditors that it (the audit) must not be limited to a stakeholder consultation exercise, we must engage with consumers of electricity,” an official said.
The exercise will capture the experiences of around 10,000 consumers across industrial, agricultural and domestic categories, with particular emphasis on the reliability and quality of power supply.

Power trading and procurement costs will constitute another major area of scrutiny. Officials pointed out that the share of short-term power procurement in states’ overall power purchase basket has risen from around 7-8% five years ago to nearly 14% currently, with power exchanges accounting for more than 56% of such transactions.
“Ultimately, the cost at which the power is purchased would impact the end consumer of the electricity, and it also impacts financials of the entities concerned,” officials said.

The audit will also examine key operational indicators, including aggregate technical and commercial (AT&C) losses, billing and collection efficiency, alongside the financial health and long-term viability of discoms.

Discoms have been selected for the first phase given their direct interface with consumers and the cascading impact of their financial and operational performance on other segments of the power sector and the wider economy.
The CAG will also rope in the coal department to facilitate an integrated assessment of the sector.

articles.title: Pakistan calls for 'immediate' end to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia at UN
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Pakistan has called for the “immediate and unconditional” cessation of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia as the UN Security Council renewed targeted sanctions under its Yemen sanctions regime for another year.
The Security Council unanimously adopted the resolution on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

According to a report in Dawn , Pakistan's Permanent Representative to the UN Ambassador Syed Haider Shah, while explaining his country's vote in favour of the resolution, said that Islamabad “condemns in the strongest terms” the continued Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia.

The Iran-backed Houthis have intensified attacks on Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, claiming strikes on oil infrastructure and military facilities, while Saudi air defences have intercepted several missiles and drones, including those targeting Riyadh.

“We stand in full and unwavering solidarity with the leadership, government, and brotherly people of Saudi Arabia. Our support for the kingdom’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, security and stability is resolute,” Mr. Shah said.

“Consistent with the United Nations Charter and international law, we support its legitimate right to defend its territory and protect its citizens and residents. We demand an immediate and unconditional cessation of these reprehensible Houthi attacks,” he said.
Mr. Shah described accountability for individuals and entities threatening Yemen’s peace, security, and stability as essential to creating conditions for lasting peace.

The resolution condemns Houthi military escalation inside Yemen, cross-border attacks against Saudi Arabia, and threats to commercial shipping, and seeks to address the group's access to dual-use components and precursor chemicals used in weapons production, the report said.

Pakistan backed stronger international action against the Houthis but stressed that the conflict required a political settlement respecting Yemen's sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity.

Mr. Shah called for an inclusive political process under UN leadership, saying an “inclusive political process that is Yemeni-owned and Yemeni-led” was necessary to advance peace and stability, as he reaffirmed Pakistan's readiness to support international efforts to restore peace and stability and address Yemen's humanitarian suffering.

The Iran-backed Houthis seized Yemen's capital Sanaa in September 2014 amid a prolonged political crisis and expanded their control over parts of the country, prompting a Saudi-led military intervention in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.

Negotiations on the resolution involved disagreements over language describing the Houthis as a terrorist group, with Britain initially seeking to restore the designation used in some previous sanctions resolutions but dropping the effort after Russia objected that it could hamper political negotiations.

articles.title: Iran says it struck U.S. military radar in Bahrain
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on Friday (November 13, 2026) said it had “destroyed” a U.S. military early-warning radar in Bahrain, in retaliation for a U.S. strike on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, southern Iran.

“An hour ago, in response to the enemy’s air attack on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, the IRGC’s aerospace fighters targeted and destroyed the early-warning radar of the American aggressors on the island of Bahrain,” the IRGC said in its statement.
It added that the attack was “a serious warning to the aggressor enemy to end air mischief and oil smuggling in the Strait of Hormuz”.
The U.S. military in recent days had carried out limited air strikes on Qeshm island and other parts of southern Iran near the strait, which it said were “defensive in nature”.

October saw a record spike in maritime attacks in the Strait of Hormuz with nearly three dozen tankers being hit. The IRGC says the strait is closed, while the U.S. Navy claims that it has opened a southern route for commercial vessels to exit and enter the critical waterway, while maintaining its “ironclad blockade” of Iranian ports. In the first week of November, at least six vessels came under attack in the strait, according to the U.K. Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO). The U.S. says its strikes in southern Iran were aimed at neutralising the threats the IRGC posed to maritime traffic.
“In case of repeated violations and aggressions, the IRGC’s air force is on full alert for borderless confrontation,” the Guards said in the statement.

The latest confrontation comes hours after U.S. President Donald Trump pulled Vice President J.D. Vance off talks with Iran, saying the U.S. did not want a deal with Iran. “Those days have long since passed. We have got their money, hundreds of billions of dollars, and we have got their strait,” he wrote in a social media post, after diplomatic efforts mediated by Qatar failed to reach any breakthrough.

Iran wants the U.S. to meet its conditions, including removal of the blockade, unfreezing of its assets and war reparation, to reopen the strait and bring the nuclear issue back to the table. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio had said earlier this week that Iran’s demands were “outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic”.

Before the November 3 U.S. midterm elections, Mr. Trump had said that he would decide whether he should “destroy” Iran based on the outcome of the diplomatic outcomes. But after the midterm, in which his Republican party suffered a massive defeat, Mr. Trump signalled that he was stepping back from renewed conflict.

Immediately after the results, Vice President J.D. Vance had blamed the war on Iran as the main reason for the Republican rout. On November 10, Mr. Trump said he would maintain the status quo on Iran — no immediate military escalation — but added that the naval blockade would stay in place. Tehran, on the other side, vowed to break the status quo.

On Friday (November 13, 2026), Iran’s chief of the general staff Maj. Gen. Ali Abdollahi said any miscalculation by the U.S. and Israel will be met with “devastating strikes”. “We warn the United States and the Zionist regime once again that the previous slaps were only the beginning of the story, and in the event of any new miscalculation, far more lethal blows await them,” he stated.

articles.title: Europe warned against falling for Russia's 'traps' on Ukraine talks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: European Union (EU) foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas warned on Friday (November 13, 2026) that Europe must not walk into Russian “traps” over Ukraine talks, saying reaching a ceasefire needed to be the priority, not broader security negotiations.

U.S. envoys said on Thursday (November 12, 2026) after talks with Vladimir Putin that Europe would join future negotiations — but the Kremlin appeared to slam the brakes on that plan saying no decision had been made.
After pushing for months to be involved, Europe is now asking itself who should represent it and what it is willing to discuss with the Kremlin.
Moscow has pushed to renegotiate Europe’s broader security architecture as part of any talks — and appears to be reviving hardline demands to roll back NATO.

“First we need a ceasefire. If we start to talk about what Russia is asking regarding the security architecture, we actually walk into the traps that Russia is setting us, which is that we divert the attention away from that there is no ceasefire,” Ms. Kallas told reporters at an EU summit in Dublin.
U.S. envoy and Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner said that getting Europe onboard will “allow us to address the broader postwar European security arrangements”.
The new push has set alarm bells ringing among U.S. allies in Europe who have long rejected the Kremlin’s desire to overhaul the continent’s security framework.
European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen insisted it was “self-explanatory that Europe is included in the peace talks to safeguard our interests, but also to support Ukraine”.
At the same time, there are calls for Europe to decide soon on who will represent it — with EU leaders set to debate the issue in Dublin.
“This needs to be resolved,” said Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin.
“In my view, finally decided upon within the next week or two.”
This week officials from Britain, France, and Germany, along with the EU, were present on the sidelines of talks in Abu Dhabi.

articles.title: Who is Jensen Huang and how the timeline of spy scandal unfolded
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Jensen Huang resigned as Chief Executive Officer of Nvidia on Thursday (November 12, 2026), bringing an end to his 33-year stint at the helm of the artificial intelligence giant he co-founded, following revelations of his extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China.

Nvidia and Mr. Huang, are also facing a proposed class-action lawsuit that accuses them of misleading shareholders by failing to disclose Mr. Huang’s alleged relationship with Alice Huang, who has been linked to Chinese intelligence.

The complaint, filed in a U.S. federal court in San Jose, California, on November 9, 2026, alleges that Nvidia and Mr. Huang concealed the relationship and the national security concerns surrounding it. Shareholders contend that the alleged omission exposed the company to reputational and business risks.

Sixty-three-year-old Taiwan-born Mr. Huang has led U.S. chipmaker Nvidia for more than three decades, transforming it into what is arguably the world’s most influential technology company. He is now at the centre of a controversy stemming from his alleged relationship with Ms. Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based firm Megaspeed and an alleged Chinese spy.

Mr. Huang was born on February 17, 1963, in Taiwan, the second son of a chemical engineer and a schoolteacher. In 1968, his family moved to Thailand before relocating to the United States amid the Vietnam War, according to Graphics News . He graduated in electrical engineering from Oregon State University and later obtained a master’s degree from Stanford University, according to his Linkedin profile.

Mr. Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife but did not disclose details about the alleged relationship with Ms. Alice Huang. The Nvidia chief executive said he was “deeply sorry” for the affair. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” he said in a statement posted on Nvidia’s website.
The New York Times reported that Ms. Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen allegedly recruited by Beijing to gather intelligence on Mr. Huang.

Mr. Huang also sent a message to Nvidia employees on November 8, 2026, acknowledging the affair and apologising to both his family and company staff. While expressing regret for his actions, he did not address allegations that Alice Huang was a suspected spy.

The Times reported last month that U.S. intelligence agencies had concluded that Mr. Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, and alleged that she was providing information directly to Beijing.

Nvidia announced a probe into the matter on November 8, 2026. Independent directors have engaged external legal counsel to examine the circumstances surrounding the relationship. Nvidia’s board said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia’s proprietary information had been compromised, and that Mr. Huang would remain in charge while cooperating with the investigation.

Ms. Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen who was allegedly recruited by Beijing to collect intelligence on the Nvidia chief executive, according to The New York Times , which first reported that Mr. Huang was the target of an alleged espionage operation.
Few public details are available about Ms. Huang, also known as Huang Le. She reportedly held a senior position at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed International.

articles.title: Experts call for coordinated action across sectors to tackle antimicrobial resistance
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) was associated with more than 4.7 million deaths in 2021, highlighting the need for coordinated action across human, animal, and environmental health sectors, experts said at the sixth Global Media Forum on AMR.

Speaking ahead of World AMR Awareness Week (November 18-24), Jean-Pierre Nyemazi, Director ai-AMR Department, World Health Organization (WHO), and Director, Quadripartite Joint Secretariat on AMR, said gaps in financing, surveillance, and coordination continued to hamper global efforts. “Behind these numbers are patients, families, farmers, and communities,” he said, stressing that global commitments should translate into results on the ground.

The updated Global Action Plan on AMR for 2026-2036 seeks to strengthen prevention, surveillance, responsible antimicrobial use and sustainable financing. World leaders have committed to reducing bacterial AMR-associated deaths by 10% by 2030.

Junxia Song, deputy chief veterinarian and chief of the One Health and Disease Control Branch, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), said antibiotic use in livestock could increase by nearly 30% by 2040 without intervention. Better animal health and farm management practices could reduce use by up to 57%.

Aitziber Echeverria, AMR coordinator, Chemicals and Health Branch, United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), called for action against environmental pollution, including antimicrobial residues in wastewater.

Kefas Samson, senior technical officer and lead of multisectoral coordination, AMR Department, WHO headquarters, highlighted gaps in diagnostics, surveillance and access to quality-assured antimicrobials. Jane Lwoyero, programme officer, World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), stressed the importance of vaccination and farm biosecurity.
Shobha Shukla, chairperson, Global AMR Media Alliance (GAMA), and host of the forum, called for a person-centred, rights-based and gender-transformative approach to tackling AMR.
The forum also recognised 56 journalists and media professionals as Global AMR Media Awardees 2026 for their contributions to reporting on antimicrobial resistance.

articles.title: Telangana Women’s Commission issues notices to eight ART centres in illegal oocyte racket case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The Telangana State Women’s Commission (TGSCW) has initiated an inquiry into an alleged illegal oocyte donation racket in Hyderabad, issuing notices to eight Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) centres and egg banks over suspected irregularities in their donor records and procurement practices.

The Commission examined representatives of the eight institutions on Friday, November 13, after directing their managements to appear before it. However, TGSCW Chairperson Nerella Sharada expressed dissatisfaction after some centres sent staff members and other representatives instead of senior management, despite being specifically instructed to attend in person. The inquiry was subsequently adjourned after the institutions assured the Commission that their management would appear at the next hearing.

During Friday’s proceedings, the Commission scrutinised reports, records and details of egg donors submitted by the ART centres and egg banks. “Several irregularities and suspicious elements have emerged from the records examined so far,” said Ms. Sharada.

She also questioned claims made by the institutions that nearly 90% of their egg donors came from other States and donated their eggs voluntarily without receiving any remuneration or financial compensation. She said the claims raised several questions and warranted further investigation.

Commissioner of Health and Family Welfare, Sangeetha Satyanarayana, also attended the inquiry, during which Ms. Sharada sought details about the progress of the department’s investigation into the alleged illegal egg procurement practices. The discussions also covered shortcomings in the existing Assisted Reproductive Technology Act and its implementation, particularly the challenges in regulating and monitoring ART centres and egg banks.

Ms. Sharada said she would soon meet Health Minister C. Damodar Raja Narasimha and Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy to inform them of the findings and discuss corrective measures, including possible legislative amendments to strengthen regulation of the sector.

Ms. Sharada further said that the Commission has also received information indicating the possible involvement of several other ART centres and egg banks in the alleged racket. It plans to issue notices to their management and summon them for questioning as part of the ongoing inquiry.

“The Commission will not tolerate illegal practices that compromise women’s health, dignity and rights. We will continue the investigation in coordination with the concerned government departments to identify those responsible and ensure appropriate legal action,” she added.

fullParagraphs: The story so far: Software giant Microsoft is facing a widespread outage affecting users of its Outlook email service, as well as its other workplace products. Thousands of Microsoft users in India awakened on Friday (November 13, 2026) to find their inboxes inaccessible, losing hours of productivity. According to DownDetector, over 100,000 users had initially registered complaints about Microsoft Outlook.​ Microsoft Outage: Why did Microsoft Outlook and other products go offline globally? Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​
Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors.

Microsoft 365 has reported improving service availability and email delivery performance across affected infrastructure, adding that there is no indication that the outage was caused by malicious or cyber activity.
The company said its teams are reviewing the incident and working to prevent similar disruptions in the future.

Microsoft says service availability is improving, with email queues significantly reduced and approaching normal levels. However, some users may continue to face intermittent access issues and delayed email delivery as the company restores affected infrastructure and monitors recovery.
Microsoft said it was seeing continued recovery progress across affected regions, with broader improvements in North America and across much of Europe.

Microsoft said service availability and email delivery were improving across a growing portion of the affected Microsoft 365 infrastructure, though some users may still face intermittent issues. It is prioritising reducing the email queue and backlog, and the extended 48-hour email timeout window stays in place to protect delayed messages.

An issue affecting Microsoft products worldwide was having a “serious impact” on Britain’s National Health Service (NHS), Rachel Harrison, public services head at the GMB union, said on Friday (November 13, 2026).

Staff receiving emergency calls were “unable to refer patient details in the normal way,” creating “a massive backlog,” though emergency and life-threatening call-outs “appear to be unaffected,” she said.
Microsoft ruled out “malicious” activity. The National Pharmacy Association said the outage was delaying prescriptions by affecting pharmacies’ communication with doctors’ offices.

Microsoft said that traffic was being gradually restored, with improvements in key customer scenarios, and that recovery actions had been completed across portions of the affected infrastructure in the Asia Pacific region. It said the focus was now on extending recovery across affected infrastructure in other regions.

“The Court is aware of the global outage affecting Microsoft systems. The Court is currently not receiving emails, but the Portal and contact forms are still functioning as normal. Parties and members of the public may not receive email notifications,” the Supreme Court of the U.K. tweeted.

articles.title: As external funding to combat TB falls, domestic spending accounts for 86%: WHO report
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Around 86% of the spending on measures against tuberculosis (TB) in 2025 came from domestic sources, the recently released Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 by the World Health Organisation (WHO) said, even as the reduction in international donor funding to combat the infectious disease remains a cause of concern.

TB cases remain one of the leading causes of death from a single infectious agent, with a quarter of all cases concentrated in India in 2025. The report notes that $22 billion is needed annually for TB prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care to achieve the global targets agreed on at the 2023 United Nations high-level TB meeting by 2027.

In absolute terms, Brazil, China, India, the Russian Federation, and South Africa accounted for $3.7 billion (65%) of the total of $5.63 billion provided from domestic sources in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).

The report notes that international donor funding fell by 14%, from $1.1 billion in 2024 to $0.94 billion in 2025, having been relatively stable at about $1.1–1.3 billion per year between 2015 and 2024.

Financing for TB research and innovation, at $1.2 billion in 2023, also continued to fall far short of the global target of $5 billion per year. Progress to date has been constrained by the overall level of investment, said the report.

“TB mostly affects adults in their most productive years. However, all age groups are at risk. Over 80% of cases and deaths are in low- and middle-income countries. In 2025, the largest number of new TB cases occurred in the WHO South-East Asia Region (35%),’’ said the report.

The WHO on Friday (November 13, 2026) called on countries in the South-East Asia Region to accelerate action to end TB. The latest TB estimates show the region accounts for 3.6 million people who developed TB in 2025 — 34% of the global total — and 4,00,000 TB-related deaths, or 35% of the global total. "These numbers are a stark reminder that TB remains one of the Region’s most pressing public health and development challenges,” said Nilesh Buddha, officer-in-charge, WHO South-East Asia Region.

A release issued by the regional office added that in 2025, $1.03 billion was available for TB prevention and care in the region, with 91% from domestic sources. Yet this represented only around 16% of global TB funding, despite the region accounting for 34% of global cases. "Closing this gap in resources is critical to sustaining progress," the WHO said.

“Ending TB is not simply a health sector responsibility. It requires leadership across government, sustained investment, strong health systems and communities at the centre of the response. We have tools to prevent, diagnose and treat TB. What is needed now is the commitment to ensure they reach everyone who needs them, without delay or financial hardship,” said Dr. Buddha, adding that ending TB by 2030 will depend on countries turning political commitments into measurable action, with greater urgency and scale.

Meanwhile, the Global TB Report said that across the world, about 50% of people treated for TB and their households face total costs (direct medical expenditures, non-medical expenditures, and indirect costs such as income losses) that are catastrophic (more than 20% of total household income). This is far from the target of the WHO End TB Strategy of zero.

In 2025, globally there were an estimated 0.96 million new TB cases that were attributable to undernutrition, 0.92 million to diabetes, 0.73 million to alcohol use disorders, 0.69 million to smoking, and 0.55 million to HIV infection.

articles.title: Aaditya Thackeray calls for Climate Change Councils at Centre, State levels to tackle pollution
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader and former Maharashtra Environment Minister Aaditya Thackeray has called for the establishment of Climate Change Councils at the Central and State levels, modelled on the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council, to ensure coordinated action against pollution and climate change.

In a post on X on Thursday, November 12, Mr. Thackeray criticised the Centre over deteriorating environmental conditions across the country and accused it of presenting misleading statistics and engaging in “greenwashing” rather than addressing the crisis.

He proposed that a central Climate Change Council be chaired by the Prime Minister and include Environment Ministers from all States. The council, he suggested, should meet every three months to review environmental data, climate targets and the progress made towards achieving them.

Mr. Thackeray also recommended including Union Ministers and representatives from departments such as urban development, rural development, energy, agriculture, industry and roads, depending on the issues under discussion.
At the State level, he proposed similar councils chaired by the respective Chief Ministers, with participation from relevant departments to monitor the implementation of climate action plans.

Referring to the ongoing COP31 climate conference in Türkiye and upcoming environmental events in Mumbai, including the Earthshot Prize and Mumbai Climate Week, Mr. Thackeray questioned the Centre’s commitment to fulfilling its international climate obligations.
He alleged that discrepancies between official environmental statistics and actual conditions had affected India’s standing on international climate indices.

Highlighting the impact of pollution on citizens, Mr. Thackeray said people were increasingly being forced to spend their own money on air purifiers, water purifiers and access to safe food despite paying direct and indirect taxes.

He also claimed that worsening environmental conditions were forcing some citizens to relocate and prompting businesses to consider leaving the country, potentially affecting employment opportunities.
Mr. Thackeray questioned whether the government was adequately addressing citizens’ basic needs, including access to clean air, safe drinking water and uncontaminated food.
He warned that failure to address climate change could have far-reaching consequences for India’s economy and national security.

Emphasising the country’s population, demographic dividend and economic potential, Mr. Thackeray said timely climate action could create significant opportunities. However, he cautioned that missing this opportunity could pose serious social, political, economic and national security risks.

articles.title: Trump administration will fund new research on controversial psychedelic drug ibogaine
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Federal officials on Thursday announced new funding to explore the medical potential of ibogaine, a controversial psychedelic drug championed by veterans, conservative lawmakers and podcasters aligned with President Donald Trump.

Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said his department is awarding up to $4.9 million to prepare for the first U.S. studies of ibogaine for post-traumatic stress disorder, a hard-to-treat condition linked to higher suicide and substance abuse rates among veterans.
The money will not go directly to patient research, Kennedy said, but to lay the groundwork needed to manufacture, dose and design studies of the drug.

Ibogaine is made from a shrub native to West Africa. It can cause intense hallucinations, nausea, vomiting, tremors and sometimes deadly irregular heart rhythms. Ibogaine is currently illegal, in the same ultra-restrictive class as LSD, ecstasy and most other psychedelic drugs.

Veterans organisations and psychedelic advocates contend that ibogaine has great promise for intractable conditions such as PTSD, severe depression and opioid addiction. U.S. research on the drug has essentially been frozen for decades due to ibogaine's restricted status.

Kennedy said the government will receive data and treatment guidance from Beond Inc., a Texas-based company that has treated more than 3,000 patients with ibogaine in Mexico, where the drug is not illegal.
“That is going to allow us to dramatically accelerate the clinical trial process,” Kennedy said. “We’re going to have, I think, a record drug approval process.”
Additional funding awards may explore ibogaine's use for addiction, he said.
Veterans Affairs Secretary Doug Collins, who joined Kennedy for the announcement, said the collaborative effort would focus first on safety and “best-in-class research.”
“For veterans living with PTSD, we owe them both urgency and the best science we can produce,” Collins said.

Kennedy and Collins have previously voiced support for the potential of psychedelics, citing the experiences of veterans who have traveled abroad for therapy with ibogaine and other mind-altering substances.

Thursday's announcement was previewed in April, when Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to speed up review and research of psychedelics that could help with mental health conditions.

articles.title: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.

The situation puts the Modi government in a spot. Ever since Ms. Hasina announced plans to return, during a virtual press conference held in Delhi on August 5 this year, Delhi-Dhaka ties have been on a downslide. The government’s decision not to prevent Ms. Hasina from addressing the press, where she used the opportunity to soundly criticise PM Rahman, meant the abrupt cancellation of the Bangladesh PM’s visit. Next month, the Indo-Bangladesh Ganga Water treaty is set to expire, and talks on its extension have also become a casualty. Ms. Hasina has been an honoured guest in India, and the government cannot physically restrain her from taking the flight to Dhaka or travelling to the land border at Petrapole to cross over. Nor can it wash its hands of her situation once she crosses over. New Delhi must redouble its diplomatic efforts on improving bilateral ties while also ensuring Ms. Hasina’s welfare.

The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.

Ever since Ms. Hasina announced plans to return, during a virtual press conference held in Delhi on August 5 this year, Delhi-Dhaka ties have been on a downslide. The government’s decision not to prevent Ms. Hasina from addressing the press, where she used the opportunity to soundly criticise PM Rahman, meant the abrupt cancellation of the Bangladesh PM’s visit. Next month, the Indo-Bangladesh Ganga Water treaty is set to expire, and talks on its extension have also become a casualty. Ms. Hasina has been an honoured guest in India, and the government cannot physically restrain her from taking the flight to Dhaka or travelling to the land border at Petrapole to cross over. articles.title: New deal: On COP31 and lofty climate goals
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The 31st Conference of Parties (COP) began this week in Antalya, Türkiye. Hosted by Türkiye and negotiations presided over by Australia, the run-up to the gathering saw ministerial delegations visit Fiji and Tuvalu. This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. However, the opening days have belied this sense of urgency. Prominent world leaders, even from the European countries who as a group champion the cause most vociferously, have chosen to skip the meet. The agenda and pre-summit expectations suggest that the main concerns this year are likely to be about delivering on existing commitments such as delivering $300 billion a year by 2035, which was decided at COP29 in Baku, as well as the COP30 call to triple the adaptation finance during that interval. However, deciding how these climate funds will practically flow has been deferred to COP32. The second global stocktake, a periodic check on progress under the Paris Agreement, begins at COP31, but the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has dithered on a timeline for the next reports that will serve as the scientific push to policy makers to accelerate efforts towards keeping a rise in temperatures below 2°C, and more ambitiously 1.5°C.

The previous edition of COP30 concluded without a formal roadmap away from fossil fuels — a step back from the COP28 consensus in Dubai. There is a voluntary roadmap ahead of COP31 but it is out of the formal negotiating text. In the background of the West Asia war, the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and financial strain writ large over Europe, funds are a challenge as evidenced in the recent Loss and Damage fund approval to Nepal of $21 million when the ask is in billions. COP31 president, Murat Kurum has laid an electrification target, which is to raise electricity’s share from 23% of total energy consumption to 35% by 2035. India has already refused to sign such a pledge and insisted on predictable climate finance, technology transfer, and nationally determined approaches to climate mitigation. These negotiations have a character of their own and deliberating nations must strive to get nations to deliver on past promises rather than commit to new lofty targets.

articles.title: Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker Prize
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.

One of the judges said she had also sought a book “only a human being could write”, but defending a novel for its ability to thumb its nose at the machines is unfair to the literary enterprise and betrays a wider public anxiety about AI, especially over the lack of consensus about its proper place in society. OpenAI has been aggravating these deliberations among mathematicians by using its machines to make headway, in record time, on problems that have been unsolved for decades, without also contributing to mathematical education and research. Anthropic , the American company known for its Claude AI model, has announced its IPO with a surprising proposed valuation of $1.4 trillion . Since much of this is pegged on speculative future demand for AI services, the same absence of consensus leaves room for investors to imagine an enormous market for Anthropic’s products and invest to help the company realise them, thus narrowing the space for society to deliberate on all competing visions of the future. And while The End of Everything , with its philosophy of pragmatic absurdism, offers poor guidance on how to keep that space open, doing so ultimately remains one of the most important unfinished tasks before the world today.

articles.title: Milking power: On the overturning of Gokul Dairy cooperative mandate
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Amid a nationwide outcry over electoral malpractices, with fresh evidence emerging every day, the BJP government in Maharashtra has gone a step further in overturning a popular mandate through an executive fiat. It approved changing the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act through an ordinance on November 4 — which the Governor promulgated on November 6 — with the immediate effect of facilitating the takeover of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul Dairy , by the BJP and its allies. A Congress-led panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the board of the cooperative on October 19. Gokul, which is one of Maharashtra’s most influential cooperative institutions, has an annual turnover of around ₹4,000 crore and is linked to several lakh milk producers in western Maharashtra. The BJP had set its eyes on the cooperative sector as yet another arena of its political dominance, creating a Ministry of Cooperation under Home Minister Amit Shah. While that plan of controlling cooperatives continues to play out through various means, the overturning of an election clearly won by the Congress-led Opposition marks a new level of brazenness by the BJP, and of the impunity its actions continue to receive from the judiciary.

The Congress-backed Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi, led by Satej Patil, won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the Gokul board. On October 29, the election of the chairman was deadlocked after the BJP-allied members did not participate, and the meeting fell short of the required quorum of 14 members. The directors allied to the Congress and its partners subsequently declared Shashikant Patil Chuyekar as chairman, but the administration refused to recognise the election as quorum requirements had not been met. The amendment made through the ordinance allowed the government to nominate five directors to certain large cooperative institutions, with four nominees receiving voting rights. To be sure, four were nominated immediately to the Gokul board, and they voted with the BJP and its partners to elect a chairman on November 10 . The mandate of the cooperative’s members had been 13-12 in favour of the Congress and its allies, but it turned 16-13 in favour of the BJP and its partners, with the appointment of members with voting rights by the State government. Those defeated approached the Bombay High Court on November 9 to restrain the government-nominated directors from voting, but the High Court did not grant that relief. The diffidence of the judiciary in intervening in favour of democratic principles is turning out to be a matter of concern . The overturning of the popular mandate in Gokul Dairy cannot be seen as an isolated incident. It is yet another instance in a troubling pattern of state power silencing the people’s choice.

articles.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

articles.title: Without any rationale: On the disbanding of the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: By abruptly disbanding the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations and handing over its task to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission, the C. Joseph Vijay government appears to have succumbed to the political impulse to reverse earlier decisions rather than being guided by any compelling rationale or necessity. This gains credence from the very grounds cited. The committee executed its mandate with scholarly rigour, seen in Part I of its report that was submitted to the then M.K. Stalin government in February. Citing the Committee’s basic character of being a “non-statutory body” is unconvincing, particularly when the Law Commission itself is established only through “executive order”. There is also no public evidence of State Law Commissions having examined or addressed issues concerning Union-State relations. The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August. Given the commission’s wider responsibilities, successive State governments had constituted high-level committees to examine conflicts involving Concurrent List subjects and recommend specific remedies. It is through such recommendations that Tamil Nadu enacted certain pieces of legislation to overcome limitations imposed by central laws, including the provision of horizontal reservation in professional course admissions for disadvantaged students. Therefore, the State’s other argument of “similarity or overlap” in the “nature and scope of the functions” entrusted to the Committee and the Commission, does not withstand close scrutiny.

In September, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, had flagged an attempt to “paralyse” the Committee’s functioning . A fair assessment of the Committee’s Part I Report reveals the breadth and depth of its dispassionate examination of issues, including State autonomy, delimitation, and the office of the Governor. Parties, barring the BJP, had largely welcomed the report. Interestingly, its contents are not even remotely at odds with the broad public ideological positioning of Mr. Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam on State rights. Besides, Prof. M. Naganathan, the Committee’s only member with an overt political association, had already resigned. The government would do well to rethink and allow it to complete its work. This would strengthen the political endeavour towards evolving a more balanced federal governance structure, facilitating harmonious Centre-State relations.

articles.title: Central Ministry removes Mahadayi basin works from online queue of pending projects
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Union government has removed the Banduri Nala diversion project in the Mahadayi river basin from the list of pending clearances from the website of the Forest Ministry.
This is believed to be due to Karnataka government’s delay in submitting responses to some queries raised by the Central team about the project.
The project was removed from the online queue of pending proposals on the PARIVESH portal of the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC).

Karnataka Neeravari Nigam Limited (KNNL) had applied for clearance to divert 71 acres of forest land for construction of pipelines, a pumphouse and powerlines in Nerse, Manturga and Bacholi villages and surrounding areas in Khanapur of Belagavi district.
Farmers, who received notices, held a meeting in Khanapur and opposed the land acquisition proposal in April 2025.
The Ministry officials conducted two field visits and issued a notice to the Congress government in the State in July 2026. But this notice did not receive an appropriate response on time.
The Central Ministry officials also indicated that a final decision on the proposal can be taken only after the Supreme Court gives a ruling in the inter-State river water dispute.

This is the first phase of the Mahadayi basin diversion works planned to provide drinking water to Hubballi-Dharwad and Gadag cities and also, some villages. The proposal for the Kalasa Nala diversion project, which is another project, is yet to be submitted to the Centre.
Karnataka forest officials say that the Banduri Nala involves lesser area of forest land submersion, compared to the Kalasa Nala project.
Meanwhile, Goa Water Resources Development Minister Subhash Shirodkar said that the Union government has withdrawn forest clearance given to Karnataka’s proposal.
He told reporters in Panaji on Friday that this move is in favour of Goa and it will strengthen his State’s case in the Supreme Court against the river basin diversion projects.
He welcomed the move and argued that Goa is opposed to the river basin projects as they can threaten the Mhadei Wildlife Sanctuary and Western Ghats ecology in general.

articles.title: Ploughing through the red tape: Inside Ambati Rayudu’s mission to fix Hyderabad cricket
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Hyderabad cricket has heard many speeches, but few came with a tractor.

In the six months since Ambati Rayudu promised to change the culture, the former India batter has been spotted pitch-side at dawn, at a soil vendor’s door in the rain and, by his own count, five to seven kilos lighter.

The initial results suggest that the effort is paying off. The first phase of this Ranji Trophy season has concluded with Hyderabad winning three matches and playing out one draw, enough to put them on top of the Elite Group B table with 20 points. The satisfaction is evident, from players to coaches.

Rayudu, the Director of Cricket Operations at the Hyderabad Cricket Association (HCA), shares that satisfaction but remains wary of premature celebrations. He takes greater pride in the systems being put in place.

“I wouldn’t read too much into the results as of now, but I’m very happy with the way the systems are set. And most importantly, the boys are very confident and glad there is something to look forward to,” he told The Hindu.

It is a long way from May 5, when he walked into a hall of cameras and vowed to take Hyderabad cricket to the next level. Plenty of people have made similar promises in those corridors. What followed, Rayudu says, was quieter than the announcement: getting the basics right, every single day.

First, he filled the calendar. Hyderabad’s age-group sides now play far more matches than the league demands, with close to a thousand match days scheduled this season. It is how his own generation grew up.
“When they wake up, if they don’t have a game, they need to be worried: ‘What am I going to do today?’ We wanted to get that feeling back.”

Wasim Jaffer’s arrival as mentor has reinforced the change, helping build a cricketing culture among players and coaches alike. Open trials now allow district players to walk into Gymkhana and compete for a State cap.
From the grassroots to the selection room, no corner of the system has escaped a rethink.

“The first point on our agenda while picking selectors was: Do they have the integrity required? Because beyond that, we will take care of whatever comes. And because they come with such integrity, they are quite adamant and stubborn in their decision making as well. That is a welcome sign because we don’t want them to be yes-men. And they have done a fantastic job, so no complaints at all. All due credit to Jeevan Reddy (HCA secretary) or anybody else, they have never questioned the team selections.”
His Cricket Operations Committee (COC) has stepped in only when it comes to choosing the team’s leadership.

articles.title: Modi recalls Mysuru Wadiyars’ contribution to science and education
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said Mysuru had a rich tradition of establishing institutions that promote knowledge, education and research, recalling the contribution of the erstwhile Mysuru rulers in building the foundation for scientific advancement.

Speaking after inaugurating the COSMOS Mysuru LED Dome Planetarium here, he said the University of Mysore was established during the reign of Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar. The Wadiyar family also played a significant role in the establishment of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) in Bengaluru. These institutions had provided generations of students and researchers with opportunities to excel, he said.

At a time when India was achieving one milestone after another in science, Mysuru was adding a new chapter to the country’s scientific journey through the state-of-the-art COSMOS Planetarium, Mr. Modi said.
“The planetarium is being dedicated today. It is India’s first LED Dome Planetarium. I had the opportunity to watch a show here. It was a remarkable experience,” he said.

Drawing a parallel between the Viveka Smaraka, which he inaugurated during his previous visit, and India’s first LED Dome Planetarium, Mr. Modi said the two institutions reflected India’s traditions of spirituality and science. While the Viveka Smaraka encouraged people to look within and explore spiritual knowledge, the planetarium inspired them to look towards the skies and understand the vast universe. “Spirituality and science have always progressed together,” he said.

Calling upon the COSMOS Planetarium authorities to encourage students to visit and experience the facility, he said, “Some of the children who visit the planetarium may one day return here to tell us about their achievements. That will be the biggest achievement of COSMOS,” he said.

Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Nirmala Sitharaman and Chief Minister D K Shivakumar also spoke. Governor Sudha Yadav, Mysuru and Kodagu MP Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar and Minister for Higher Education Basavaraj Rayareddi were present.
Earlier, Mr. Modi paid his respects to Goddess Chamundeshwari and greeted the people of Mysuru.
